detail.title: Predictive Processing and Temporal Structure in Musical Experience
detail.summary: This journal entry synthesizes the ASAP (Action Simulation for Auditory Prediction) hypothesis with interoceptive inference frameworks to examine music perception. Evidence indicates that music acts as a sequence of controlled hallucinations where the brain minimizes prediction error relative to temporal expectations. This synthesis provides a formal basis for the emotional and cognitive engagement observed in musical experiences, shifting the focus from passive stimulus-response to active, error-minimizing temporal prediction.
